title: Excuse me, where's the post office?
goal: Ask strangers for directions and understand the answer — a skill that decides whether you can get around Taiwan on your own.
bekal: ask for directions with the right opener and catch the answer
use the direction verbs 往, 過, 轉, 走
give distances with 大概 and landmarks with 看到

dialogs.title: 對話 — 迷路了
dialogs.intro: Budi is lost looking for the post office in Tainan's old town. He asks a woman selling fruit.

notes: ⚠️ **請問 is the essential opener when asking a stranger something.** Asking directly without 請問 sounds like an interrogation. The most natural combination is **不好意思，請問…** — two layers of politeness at once.
**Giving fruit or food to strangers is a living custom in Taiwan**, especially in small towns and markets. Refusing can actually offend; accept it while saying *太不好意思了* and *謝謝*.
**得 in 說得很好 marks how something is done**: verb + 得 + adjective. 說得很好 (speaks well), 跑得很快 (runs fast), 吃得很多 (eats a lot). ⚠️ It's pronounced *de*, just like 的, but written differently.
**看得到 means "can be seen"** — a potential complement, covered in unit 18. Its opposite is 看不到 (can't be seen). This pattern comes up constantly in directions.
⚠️ **芭樂 (guava) is the most everyday fruit in Taiwan**, often sold sliced with sweet-and-sour plum powder. In slang, 芭樂 also means "cheesy, cliché": *芭樂歌* = a run-of-the-mill pop song.

grammars.title: Direction verbs: 往, 過, 轉, 走
body: Directions in Mandarin are built from a few verbs that always come in the same order: **往 + direction**, then **走**, then a landmark, then **轉**.
after: **十字路口 ("road mouth shaped like the character ten") means an intersection** — 十 really is shaped like a cross. A good example of how Chinese characters help you remember words.
⚠️ **往 is always followed by a direction, not a place**: 往前 (forward), 往左 (to the left), 往北 (northward). For places, use 去 or 到.

grammars.title: 以前 and 以後: after the noun, not before
body: English says "**before** eating" and "**after** eating" with the word in front. Mandarin puts it **after** — just like the position words in unit 7.

head: 中文
Pīnyīn
Literally
Meaning
rows: ⚠️ 以前 alone = in the past

after: ⚠️ **When 以前 and 以後 stand alone at the start of a sentence, their meaning changes** to "in the past" and "in the future". *以前我不會說中文* = "I used to not speak Chinese".
**The same pattern applies to 的時候 ("when…")**: 吃飯的時候 (when eating), 小的時候 (when I was little). They all attach at the end.

head: 中文
Pīnyīn
English
rows: kěyǐ bāng wǒ kàn dìtú ma?
Could you help me with the map?

blocks.text: ⚠️ **離 (*lí*) means "at a distance from"** and the order is A 離 B + far/near: *我家離學校很近* ("my place is close to campus"). Don't confuse it with 從 (from, the starting point of a movement): *我從家裡走路去* ("I walk there from home").

⚠️ **The Mandarin order of compass points is 東西南北** (east-west-south-north), not north-east-south-west. And big street names in Taiwan often include their direction: 忠孝**東**路 (Zhongxiao Road **East**), 中山**北**路 (Zhongshan Road **North**) — very helpful when you're lost.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **You'll hear the last two questions every time you buy something at a 便利商店.** The answer: *要* or *不用，謝謝*. Plastic bags in Taiwan cost money (1–3 塊) since free bags were banned, so bring your own.
